extraction.name: PIQA: Reasoning about Physical Commonsense in Natural Language
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning in natural language, formulated as multiple-choice question answering over goal-solution pairs.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk; Rowan Zellers; Ronan Le Bras; Jianfeng Gao; Yejin Choi
extraction.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Annotators were prompted with links to instructables.com and asked to glance at the instructions, then construct two component tasks by articulating a physical goal and how to achieve it. They also provided a permutation of their own solution that would make it invalid. Additional qualification and validation HITs were used, and examples with low agreement were removed.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: How-to instructions from instructables.com were used as the source scaffold for annotation prompts; the website is described as a crowdsourced collection of instructions for doing everything from cooking to car repair.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was further cleaned of basic artifacts using the AFLite algorithm to remove stylistic artifacts and trivial examples; train, development, and test folds were automatically produced by AFLite.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Examples with low agreement were removed during validation; annotators had to pass a qualification HIT with over 80% accuracy; examples were truncated at 150 tokens for model experiments.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were asked to provide a physical goal, a valid solution, and a trick solution that sounded reasonable but was wrong, often by subtle changes such as negation, numerical changes, or swapping a key action/item. Two examples were drawn per instructable to encourage precise articulation of preconditions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Mechanical Turk (HITs); onturkerview.com is mentioned for self-reported pay information.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed. Human performance was computed by majority vote. Annotators who achieved at least 90% on the qualification HIT were selected for human evaluation.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 solution choices per item (one correct and one trick); the paper also states that annotators were asked for 1 physical goal, 1 valid solution, and 1 trick.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: AFLite; BERT-Large embeddings were used within AFLite; SpaCy and GPT BPE tokenization were used for statistics; the transformers library was used for experiments.
